verdict: Red 8/10 ACCEPT-WITH-CUTS, blue 8/10 SUSTAINED with one reduction - concordant, and the rare case where both benches agree the court itself was not worth convening. The triage scored CSHR 6/10 and was candid that a court would most likely convert a screen reading '2.8x P/E deep value' into 'roughly 5.6x trailing, 8x trough-forward crypto-beta annuity at 1.34x book, RP_FAIR at best, no edge' - a real sizing change, but one pointing to a smaller position rather than a larger one. Red went further and marked court-worthiness down from 6/10 to about 3/10, blue concurred, and I concur: the marginal sizing decision a full court changes here is nil until the company posts an actual AUM datum. The triage's best work was catching that the screen's cheapness signal is substantially a data artifact. Public screeners show P/E 2.81 and P/B 0.69 by running the pre-exchange 65.54M share count against a company with 131,780,209 shares outstanding; corrected, FY25 EPS is about $0.87 for roughly 5.6x trailing, and net assets of $481.4M give BVPS of about $3.65 for roughly 1.34x book. The same screener's 'EBITDA -$684M' is the consolidated ETP certificate liability - $4.5B of customer assets - leaking into the metric. The triage also correctly identified the $10.43 52-week high as the Vine Hill SPAC TRUST price, not an operating-company mark, so a chunk of the dd52 is mechanical: the deal closed 2026-03-31 at $1.2B over 131.78M shares, an approximately $9.10 reference. Red then killed the triage's two comfort legs, and this is the substance of the court. First, the floor is fictitious. The triage anchored comfort at 1.0-1.34x book, treating the $3.51 52-week low as a clean floor at roughly 1.0x. But of the $481.3M of 'available capital', only $176.7M is liquid - $280.0M is ACCRUED CoinShares XBT management fees, an unrealized receivable owed by the issuer's own legacy vehicles and economically linked to the XBT platform. That is 58.2% of book, confirmed verbatim by blue at $280,020 thousand. The triage's own cite - 'digital assets held as treasury $33.4M versus $481.4M net assets' - measured the wrong line entirely. Second, revenue is not arithmetically 170bps times AUM. Capital Markets revenue and gains are $73.1M, roughly 37% of total, including $21.9M of staking and $10.7M of lending. Blue sustained this with a useful nuance red overstated: Capital Markets fell 11.6% in an UP year, so 'reverses hardest in a crypto winter' is inference rather than established - but the triage's arithmetic omitting 37% of revenue is refuted regardless. Net income already fell from $162.4M to $114.3M, down 30%, in a rising year. Both the E and the B in the cheapness math are crypto-beta; there is no hard-asset floor at $3.51, only a smaller version of the same bet. Third, the supply overhang is confirmed and precise: 105,610,080 resale shares plus 10,999,993 warrant shares at an $11.50 strike registered via F-1 on 5/15, effective 6/02, 424B3 on 6/03 - roughly 80% of the share count registered for sale within ten weeks of the SPAC close, against an ADV around 84k shares. The warrants are out of the money, so the per-share math itself survives the cap-structure check. Blue's one REDUCTION is instructive and lands on red rather than the thesis: red claimed the monthly AUM cadence was 'a promise, not a feed' because no July or August posting existed on the IR press feed. Red checked the wrong venue - the tracker is not on the press feed, it lives at investor.coinshares.com/financials#aum, and the 7/30 release's operative language is present tense ('publishes... updated no later than the third business day of each month... continue to provide'), i.e. a live commitment. The tracker content is JS-rendered and unreachable to the fetcher, so whether July data is posted is UNVERIFIED. Red's absence claim was itself an instrument artifact - the same error class the blue bench exists to catch, applied to the prosecution. Blue also added a genuinely two-sided finding red used only negatively: the pending buyback authority. Authorized repurchases against a 105.6M-share overhang at roughly 1x hard-adjusted book would be accretive and are management's stated intent, so the EGM date is a tripwire rather than merely an absence. And blue flagged an unbounded tail neither bench closed: $10.7M of lending interest implies principal deployed to crypto counterparties in a drawdown, which the H1 balance sheet resolves. On doctrine: this is not a kill of the business, it is a fairness-unverifiable ruling. RP_FAIR would make CSHR ownable only with fairness VERIFIED and tails bounded, and both of the relevant B's - book quality and the flow leg - are unverifiable until the first real AUM datum and the H1 balance sheet. That is a gate, not a kill of the name; but as of today it is a no-touch, and the book is already flat, so nothing changes.
reopen_gates: First VERIFIABLE monthly AUM and net-flow posting (the tracker at investor.coinshares.com/financials#aum, JS-rendered - needs Playwright/real-Chrome, not WebFetch; both benches failed on it). Requires net INFLOWS with a blended yield at or above 160bps. This is the single highest-value missing input and it is already public.

H1-2026 results, due no later than 2026-09-30 per the company's own 7/30 release: balance sheet showing whether the $280.0M accrued XBT fee receivable is denominated or hedged in fiat and actually realizable. If it marks with crypto, the book-value floor stays fictitious at any price.

H1 balance sheet bounding the lending book - blue's unclosed tail: $10.7M of lending interest implies principal deployed to crypto counterparties during a 49% drawdown in the underlying. Neither bench bounded this and it is a solvency-adjacent question, not a sizing one.

424B3 selling-shareholder lockup terms verified as extending past the H1 results (the F-1 was too large to fetch - UNVERIFIED on both benches). 105,610,080 registered resale shares against roughly 84k shares/day of volume is years of supply if unlocked.

EGM notice and buyback authority - blue's two-sided tripwire. Authorized repurchases against the overhang at roughly 1x hard-adjusted book would be accretive; the notice was promised 'shortly' on 7/30 and as of the court had still not published.
Do NOT re-fire the dislocation screen on the raw dd52: the $10.43 52-week high is the Vine Hill SPAC trust price, not an operating mark, so part of the drawdown is mechanical.
